slides.caption: One feature file doubled in size and a fixed 200-feature limit turned it into a global 5xx event
slides.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720" font-family="Arial" data-pptx-page-role="content">
  <rect id="page-field" data-pptx-role="background" x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF" />
  <g id="page-header" data-pptx-bounds="64 60 1152 100">
    <text x="64" y="92" font-size="36" font-weight="bold" fill="#1F2933">One feature file doubled in size and a fixed 200-feature<tspan x="64" dy="43">limit turned it into a global 5xx event</tspan></text>
    <line x1="64" y1="158" x2="1216" y2="158" stroke="#D7DDE3" stroke-width="1" />
  </g>
  <g id="summary-lead" data-pptx-bounds="64 166 1152 70">
    <text x="64" y="190" font-size="26" fill="#1F2933">The failure was in the ingestion of Cloudflare’s own generated<tspan x="64" dy="36">configuration, not in the traffic that configuration governs.</tspan></text>
  </g>
  <g id="moment-change-deployed" data-pptx-bounds="64 246 264 122">
    <use data-icon="chunk-filled/circle-minus" x="64" y="248" width="12" height="12" fill="#4A5568" />
    <text x="82" y="258" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#5A6673">NORMAL · CHANGE DEPLOYED</text>
    <text x="64" y="316" font-family="Consolas" font-size="56" font-weight="bold" fill="#4A5568">11:05</text>
    <text x="64" y="342" font-size="16" fill="#5A6673">Database access control<tspan x="64" dy="20">change deployed</tspan></text>
  </g>
  <g id="moment-impact-starts" data-pptx-bounds="360 246 264 122">
    <use data-icon="chunk-filled/circle-x" x="360" y="248" width="12" height="12" fill="#B4342C" />
    <text x="378" y="258" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#5A6673">CRITICAL · IMPACT STARTS</text>
    <text x="360" y="316" font-family="Consolas" font-size="56" font-weight="bold" fill="#B4342C">11:28</text>
    <text x="360" y="342" font-size="16" fill="#5A6673">First errors observed on<tspan x="360" dy="20">customer HTTP traffic</tspan></text>
  </g>
  <g id="moment-main-resolved" data-pptx-bounds="656 246 264 122">
    <use data-icon="chunk-filled/triangle-exclamation" x="656" y="248" width="12" height="12" fill="#B7791F" />
    <text x="674" y="258" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#5A6673">DEGRADED · MAIN IMPACT ENDS</text>
    <text x="656" y="316" font-family="Consolas" font-size="56" font-weight="bold" fill="#B7791F">14:30</text>
    <text x="656" y="342" font-size="16" fill="#5A6673">Correct configuration file<tspan x="656" dy="20">deployed globally</tspan></text>
  </g>
  <g id="moment-all-resolved" data-pptx-bounds="952 246 264 122">
    <use data-icon="chunk-filled/circle-checkmark" x="952" y="248" width="12" height="12" fill="#2E7D5B" />
    <text x="970" y="258" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#5A6673">RECOVERED · ALL RESOLVED</text>
    <text x="952" y="316" font-family="Consolas" font-size="56" font-weight="bold" fill="#2E7D5B">17:06</text>
    <text x="952" y="342" font-size="16" fill="#5A6673">All downstream services<tspan x="952" dy="20">restarted and restored</tspan></text>
  </g>
  <g id="fact-trigger" data-pptx-bounds="64 400 552 112">
    <text x="64" y="412" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#B4342C">TRIGGER</text>
    <text x="64" y="442" font-size="20" fill="#1F2933">A change to one of Cloudflare’s database<tspan x="64" dy="30">systems’ permissions made the query output</tspan><tspan x="64" dy="30">duplicate entries into the feature file.</tspan></text>
  </g>
  <g id="fact-mechanism" data-pptx-bounds="664 400 552 112">
    <text x="664" y="412" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#B4342C">MECHANISM</text>
    <text x="664" y="442" font-size="20" fill="#1F2933">The file doubled in size and passed the<tspan x="664" dy="30">bots module’s preallocated limit of 200</tspan><tspan x="664" dy="30">features, against roughly 60 then in use.</tspan></text>
  </g>
  <g id="fact-scope" data-pptx-bounds="64 548 552 112">
    <text x="64" y="560" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#B4342C">SCOPE</text>
    <text x="64" y="590" font-size="20" fill="#1F2933">Core CDN and security services, Turnstile,<tspan x="64" dy="30">Workers KV, Dashboard, Email Security and</tspan><tspan x="64" dy="30">Access were affected, in different ways.</tspan></text>
  </g>
  <g id="fact-recovery" data-pptx-bounds="664 548 552 112">
    <text x="664" y="560" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#B4342C">RECOVERY</text>
    <text x="664" y="590" font-size="20" fill="#1F2933">Core traffic was largely flowing as normal<tspan x="664" dy="30">by 14:30, and all remaining services were</tspan><tspan x="664" dy="30">restored at 17:06.</tspan></text>
  </g>
  <g id="page-footer" data-pptx-bounds="64 680 1152 22" fill="#5A6673" font-size="12">
    <text x="64" y="692">Cloudflare, “Cloudflare outage on November 18, 2025”. All times UTC.</text>
    <text x="1216" y="692" text-anchor="end">02</text>
  </g>
</svg>

    <text x="64" y="470" font-size="20" fill="#1F2933">This also affected Workers KV and Access,<tspan x="64" dy="30">which rely on the core proxy.</tspan></text>

slides.caption: Four conditions had to hold at once, and no single one of them is the cause
slides.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720" font-family="Arial" data-pptx-page-role="content">
  <rect id="page-field" data-pptx-role="background" x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
  <g id="page-header" data-pptx-bounds="64 60 1152 100">
    <text x="64" y="92" font-size="36" font-weight="bold" fill="#1F2933">Four conditions had to hold at once, and no<tspan x="64" dy="43">single one of them is the cause</tspan></text>
    <line x1="64" y1="158" x2="1216" y2="158" stroke="#D7DDE3" stroke-width="1"/>
  </g>
  <g id="p10-factor-assumption" data-pptx-bounds="64 180 1152 108">
    <rect x="64" y="180" width="4" height="108" fill="#B4342C"/>
    <text x="84" y="198" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#B4342C">TECHNICAL</text>
    <text x="230" y="206" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#1F2933">An assumption about the query’s scope was never restated</text>
    <text x="230" y="254" font-size="16" fill="#1F2933">The feature-generation query assumed table metadata would only ever be returned for the<tspan x="230" dy="22">default database. That assumption was not revisited when the permissions model changed at 11:05.</tspan></text>
  </g>
  <g id="p10-factor-limit" data-pptx-bounds="64 296 1152 108">
    <rect x="64" y="296" width="4" height="108" fill="#B4342C"/>
    <text x="84" y="314" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#B4342C">TECHNICAL</text>
    <text x="230" y="322" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#1F2933">A fixed limit guarded memory but had no bounded failure path</text>
    <text x="230" y="370" font-size="16" fill="#1F2933">The bots module preallocates memory for at most 200 machine-learning features. An input above<tspan x="230" dy="22">that limit produced an unhandled error and a thread panic, not a rejected file or a degraded score.</tspan></text>
  </g>
  <g id="p10-factor-validation" data-pptx-bounds="64 412 1152 108">
    <rect x="64" y="412" width="4" height="108" fill="#B7791F"/>
    <text x="84" y="430" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#B7791F">PROCEDURAL</text>
    <text x="230" y="438" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#1F2933">Cloudflare-generated configuration was trusted more than user input</text>
    <text x="230" y="486" font-size="16" fill="#1F2933">The first published remediation item is to harden ingestion of Cloudflare-generated configuration<tspan x="230" dy="22">files in the same way as user-generated input — which states that, before this incident, it was not.</tspan></text>
  </g>
  <g id="p10-factor-propagation" data-pptx-bounds="64 528 1152 108">
    <rect x="64" y="528" width="4" height="108" fill="#B7791F"/>
    <text x="84" y="546" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#B7791F">PROCEDURAL</text>
    <text x="230" y="554" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#1F2933">The change propagated gradually, so the failure looked like an attack</text>
    <text x="230" y="602" font-size="16" fill="#1F2933">Only the updated part of the ClickHouse cluster produced bad data, so output alternated every<tspan x="230" dy="22">five minutes and the failure signature resembled an attack rather than a deployment.</tspan></text>
  </g>

    <text x="230" y="206" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#1F2933">Internally generated configuration reaches every machine in minutes</text>
    <text x="230" y="254" font-size="16" fill="#1F2933">Both outages began inside Cloudflare’s own configuration path, and in both the step that made a local<tspan x="230" dy="22">defect global was the same. Naming that shared condition is an inference across two published accounts.</tspan></text>

    <text x="64" y="388" font-size="16" fill="#1F2933">A new WAF managed rule containing a regular expression<tspan x="64" dy="22">that backtracked enormously and exhausted CPU worldwide.</tspan></text>
    <text x="64" y="438" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#5A6673">PROPAGATION</text>
    <text x="64" y="460" font-size="16" fill="#1F2933">Pushed through Quicksilver, which distributes changes<tspan x="64" dy="22">globally in seconds; by design the WAF skipped the</tspan><tspan x="64" dy="22">staged rollout process.</tspan></text>
    <text x="64" y="532" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#5A6673">MITIGATION</text>
    <text x="64" y="554" font-size="16" fill="#1F2933">A global kill switch — a “global terminate” — executed<tspan x="64" dy="22">at 14:07; traffic and CPU normal again by 14:09.</tspan></text>

    <text x="656" y="388" font-size="16" fill="#1F2933">A database permissions change that made the Bot<tspan x="656" dy="22">Management feature file more than double in size.</tspan></text>
    <text x="656" y="438" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#5A6673">PROPAGATION</text>
    <text x="656" y="460" font-size="16" fill="#1F2933">The feature file is refreshed every few minutes and<tspan x="656" dy="22">published to the entire network so the model can react</tspan><tspan x="656" dy="22">to new bots and new bot attacks.</tspan></text>
    <text x="656" y="532" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#5A6673">MITIGATION</text>
    <text x="656" y="554" font-size="16" fill="#1F2933">No per-feature kill switch is described; the remediation<tspan x="656" dy="22">commits to enabling more global kill switches.</tspan></text>

# Cloudflare Outage Postmortem - Design Spec

## I. Project Information

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Project Name | cloudflare_outage_postmortem |
| Canvas Format | PPT 16:9 (1280×720) |
| Page Count | 15 |
| Primary Language | en |
| Target Audience | Site-reliability and platform engineers, incident commanders, and the engineering leaders they report to, at organizations whose availability depends on Cloudflare; secondary readers are reliability reviewers who will reuse this account as a worked example of a blameless postmortem. They know what a reverse proxy and a config rollout are; they have not read the 22,000-character source post. |
| Communication Intent | Record and hand off first: establish an accurate, source-anchored account of the 18 November 2025 Cloudflare outage that can be cited without reopening the blog. Then explain the mechanism by which a database permissions change became a global HTTP 5xx event. Then align readers on which conditions persist, which corrective actions Cloudflare committed to, and which questions the published account leaves open. Never argue about fault. |
| Desired Audience Outcome | A reader who was not there can restate the trigger, the mechanism, the impact window, and the detection-versus-diagnosis gap from memory; can tell an observed fact from an inference and from an unconfirmed item; and can name both the corrective actions and what the published account does not settle. |
| Core Message / Ask / Action | A routine database permissions change at 11:05 UTC doubled a Bot Management feature file; a fixed 200-feature preallocation limit turned that oversized file into an unhandled panic in the core proxy; the failure was detected in three minutes but took nearly three hours to diagnose because a five-minute regeneration cycle made it look like an attack. The condition that made it global — internally generated configuration propagated worldwide without staged rollout or consumer-side validation — is the same condition behind the 2 July 2019 outage. |
| Delivery Context | Primary: reader-led. A written postmortem circulated asynchronously and read end to end by people who were not in the incident channel. Secondary: presented in a 30-minute incident-review meeting where the timeline and corrective-action pages are projected. |
| Artifact Afterlife | Review, audit, and archive. Individual pages — the summary, the timeline, the corrective actions — will be quoted and forwarded on their own, so each must stand alone. Reused as a structural reference for internal postmortems. |
| Reading Mode | text |
| Content Strategy | Stay close. Every number, timestamp, product name, identifier, and quoted string comes from the published Cloudflare accounts of 18 November 2025 and 2 July 2019. Nothing is estimated, rounded for effect, or supplied from outside those two documents; where the source does not state a value, the page says NO DATA or marks the item unconfirmed. Elapsed durations are arithmetic on published timestamps and are labeled as derived. |
| Design Style | Incident Postmortem method (installed Style workspace) realized as a neutral achromatic record: white field, hairline rules, a fixed left-to-right time direction, and colour reserved entirely for the four declared severity states, each always paired with a text label. |
| AI Image Acquisition Path | not applicable |
| Generation Mode | continuous |
| Spec Refinement | disabled |
| Speaker Notes | enabled — workflow default (no explicit user instruction; proactive Stage-2 value `true`) |
| Custom Animations | enabled — explicit user instruction: the deck must carry a hand-authored `animations.json` with at least two Morph pairs |
| Narration Audio | disabled — workflow default |
| Created Date | 2026-09-05 |

- **Template Application**: The installed `incident-postmortem` Style supplies the communication method and the design defaults, and nothing else — it owns no structure, so every page is composed freely and flat. Adopted deliberately: its argument flow (facts, then interpretation, then action), its claim discipline (observed event / inferred sequence / contributing factor / hypothesis kept distinct, unconfirmed items marked, systems and roles named instead of people), its page-role vocabulary as the roster's skeleton, its evidence rules (one timestamp precision and one stated time zone throughout, native editable tables for timeline and actions, no redrawn monitoring graph presented as the record), its restraint defaults (effectively no decoration, colour only for declared severity, always with a label), and its Fallback Colour Scheme and typographic character (plain neutral sans plus a genuinely monospaced companion) — taken as identity because no Brand or Deck workspace is active. Two Style tendencies are deliberately not followed: its `digital-dashboard` image rendering and its evidence-image guidance are inert because this deck carries no images at all (the only legitimate evidence images are Cloudflare's copyrighted screenshots), and its instruction to keep monitoring graphs as captured evidence rather than redrawing them is honoured by labelling the one time-series page a schematic reconstruction rather than a record. Its Review Focus section is not activated.

## III. Visual Theme

### Theme Style

- **Mode**: briefing
- **Visual style**: swiss-minimal
- **Theme**: A record, not a report about a record. A white field with a strict two-band grid, hairline rules instead of boxes, and a time direction that never changes: earlier is always left, later is always right, on the chart, on the timeline tables, and on the severity strip that runs across the deck. The only chromatic events on any page are the four declared severity states.
- **Tone**: Factual, unhurried, and unembarrassed. The account describes what responders could see at each moment; it never uses hindsight vocabulary and never attributes an outcome to a person.
